title: backlog.py brief ID prints the worker's brief and dispatch ID starts the headless worker from it
goal: python3 _tools/backlog.py brief ID prints the brief the kb-sprint skill's run step 3 now composes by hand: the item's JSON and goal text, its external tracker ids with their urls (ST-vkqndn5e's helper), the role file path, the scratch directory, the in-flight sibling items with the files their touches change, the known failing tests the orchestrator names (--known TEST=BUG), the fixed worker rules (own checks, no tests.py --changed, the test ceiling, commit on work/<id> with KB-Work, never push, foreground tests, file bugs outside the item, gates for open choices) and the rules of the docs its touches map to (rag.py pack --root _self --item ID on the kb). python3 _tools/backlog.py dispatch ID makes the scratch directory _cache/scratch/<id>/, writes the brief there and starts claude -p --model sonnet --effort high --output-format json --add-dir <scratch> --max-turns <by kind: 60 task or subtask, 100 bug or untasked story, 200 research story or investigation bug> with the brief on stdin, never as a prompt argument (SP-d3hybrlv), records the session id and the pid on the item's claim, and with --dry-run prints the argv and the brief path without starting; --model names another model only when given. The kb-sprint skill's run step 3 shrinks to the two commands.

gates.question: Does dispatch make the worker's worktree, or require that the orchestrator made it?
options: dispatch makes it when absent: git worktree add <worktree_dir>/agent-ID -b work/ID from this checkout's HEAD (a branch that exists is checked out instead), and reuses one that is there
dispatch requires it: it refuses an absent worktree (exit 2) naming the git worktree add command, and the orchestrator keeps making it by hand
gates.recommendation: dispatch makes it when absent: git worktree add <worktree_dir>/agent-ID -b work/ID from this checkout's HEAD (a branch that exists is checked out instead), and reuses one that is there

gates.question: Does dispatch run the session in the foreground or detached, and where does its JSON output go?
options: foreground: dispatch waits until the session exits, writes its --output-format json output to SCRATCH/result.json and stderr to SCRATCH/stderr.log, and exits 0 only when the session exited 0 without is_error; the orchestrator starts dispatch as a background command and is told at its exit
detached: dispatch starts the session as a child that outlives it, same output files, and returns at once; the orchestrator polls the recorded pid
gates.recommendation: foreground: dispatch waits until the session exits, writes its --output-format json output to SCRATCH/result.json and stderr to SCRATCH/stderr.log, and exits 0 only when the session exited 0 without is_error; the orchestrator starts dispatch as a background command and is told at its exit

gates.question: Where are the session id and the pid recorded on the item's claim, and under which field names? The kb names no flag that fixes the session id up front (public/claude/cli-flags.csv lists --output-format json, --resume and --max-turns only; ci-and-headless.md:74 DOC S-fmj24q2u: session_id is a field of the result message), and a search of the live Claude Code docs on 2026-10-10 found none either, so the id is known when the session ends
options: the clone's claims ledger in the git dir (kb-backlog-claims.json, which claim writes and git never commits), on the item's record: worker_pid when the session starts, worker_session when it exits

item-file fields beside claimed_by, committed with the item: needs bl_base ORDER, bl_check, bl_items and bl_land, outside this item's touches, and puts a GUID-shaped session id into published item files
a dispatch.json in the scratch directory, apart from the claim
gates.recommendation: the clone's claims ledger in the git dir (kb-backlog-claims.json, which claim writes and git never commits), on the item's record: worker_pid when the session starts, worker_session when it exits

gates.question: What --max-turns does dispatch give an epic or a sprint, kinds the goal names no cap for?
options: 100, the cap of a bug or an untasked story: an epic's worker breaks it down into stories as an untasked story's does
200, the cap of a research story or an investigation bug
gates.recommendation: 100, the cap of a bug or an untasked story: an epic's worker breaks it down into stories as an untasked story's does

gates.question: How does dispatch know a bug is an investigation bug (200 turns) and a story a research story, given no item field marks either?
options: a story is a research story when it is the goal research story or its scope is kb content only (bl_base.research_touches); a bug is an investigation bug when its title or goal holds the word investigat; dispatch --max-turns N overrides the cap for any other
dispatch --max-turns N only: the orchestrator names 200 itself and the kind gives 60 or 100
gates.recommendation: a story is a research story when it is the goal research story or its scope is kb content only (bl_base.research_touches); a bug is an investigation bug when its title or goal holds the word investigat; dispatch --max-turns N overrides the cap for any other

gates.question: What format is the brief, and how is it printed and written?
options: Markdown text in sections (item with its JSON and goal text, external ids, staging copies, in-flight siblings, known failing tests, fixed rules, rules of the docs, report); brief prints it through the name guard, dispatch writes it unguarded to SCRATCH/brief.md so the paths stay usable; --probe TEXT adds an unproven bug's probe result
a JSON object with one key per part, which the session reads as data
gates.recommendation: Markdown text in sections (item with its JSON and goal text, external ids, staging copies, in-flight siblings, known failing tests, fixed rules, rules of the docs, report); brief prints it through the name guard, dispatch writes it unguarded to SCRATCH/brief.md so the paths stay usable; --probe TEXT adds an unproven bug's probe result

gates.question: Does dispatch --dry-run write the brief and make the scratch directory, or only print?
options: it only prints the worktree, scratch, brief path and argv, and makes and writes nothing (brief prints the text)
it writes SCRATCH/brief.md and makes the scratch directory so the brief can be read at the printed path, and makes no worktree and starts nothing
gates.recommendation: it only prints the worktree, scratch, brief path and argv, and makes and writes nothing (brief prints the text)
